fact_text: Pakistan's mutual fund industry had about 4.5 trillion in assets under management as of May 2026, against roughly 3.9 trillion around June 2025 (figures as stated by the interviewee).
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Pakistan's mutual fund assets under management grew from under 1 trillion in 2021 to about 4.5 trillion, a compound annual growth rate of roughly 35% over 2021-2026.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Pakistan's mutual fund industry is only about 0.02% of global mutual fund assets, which the interviewee put at roughly 85 trillion dollars.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Pakistan's voluntary pension scheme (VPS) industry had about 138 billion in assets, a very small segment of the 4.5 trillion mutual fund industry, per the interviewee.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Pakistan's savings rate was about 21-22% of GDP in 1990, level with India's, but it fell sharply afterwards while India's rose to about 30%, according to the interviewee.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: The interviewee argued that low household savings and low disposable income are the main reason the mutual fund industry is small relative to the economy.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Mutual fund money enters only through the banking channel, so a large informal economy that stays outside banks keeps the fund industry's share of GDP small, according to the interviewee.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Banks earn a 4-5% spread on deposits, while the average mutual fund fee is about 1%, so the interviewee said bankers have little incentive to sell fund products and branch networks often discourage them.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: The securities regulator caps mutual fund charges, which can go up to about 3% for equity funds, but the interviewee said the real average expense ratio across Pakistani funds is below 1%, not 5%.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: The average expense ratio of Pakistani mutual funds is below 1% per year, and the interviewee said no extra fees beyond the disclosed charge apply to investors.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: The interviewee compared a fund manager to a doctor: the manager profiles risk, return target, liquidity and wealth needs and picks the product, which is the value that justifies the fee.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Pakistan's asset-management menu includes equity, energy, dividend-yield, money market, income, REIT, fixed-term and pension funds, and the interviewee said fund managers match each investor's risk profile to one of them.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: An investor's risk profile and asset allocation change with age, so the interviewee said a fund manager should reassess allocation periodically as the investor moves toward retirement.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Inflation of about 10% leaves money market funds, which earn around 10%, with a very low real return, and the 15-20% tax on that income reduces the effective return further, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: The interviewee said the Pakistan stock market has returned about 19% a year on average over 30 years to 2026, the highest return among local assets such as property, gold, dollars and fixed income, though volatile.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: The interviewee said the market's dividend yield is about 6-7% and earnings growth is about 12-13% in 2026, and that a sustainable return of 19-20% is possible if the market is re-rated.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: The interviewee said the market's valuation multiple is about 6 to 6.5 times, and that a re-rating to 8 times would add roughly 20% to prices.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Fixed-return mutual funds with fixed lock-in periods of one or three months have grown to about 10% of the industry, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Institutional money is moving from money market funds into equity funds as investors see the market as stable with higher returns, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Islamic funds rose from zero or about 1% of the mutual fund industry in its early years to about 49% of assets, according to the interviewee.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Islamic mutual funds grew about 42% a year on average over 2021-2026, against about 35% for conventional funds, and the interviewee said the Islamic share could be 70-75% if enough sukuk were available.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: The KMI-30 Islamic index earned a marginally higher return than the conventional KSE-100 index over about 20 years, and over 20-25 year periods the two returns were similar, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: The government decided that the whole financial sector would be made Islamic by 2027, and the interviewee said this has made government sukuk issuance more regular and larger in size.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Limited sukuk supply capped the growth of Islamic funds in early years, according to the interviewee, and the interviewee expected supply constraints to ease as government sukuk issuance grows.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: A tax credit of up to 2 million on mutual fund investments, with a two-year lock-in, was discontinued, the interviewee said, removing an incentive for long-term saving.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: A graded capital gains tax, which was zero after holding for about four to six years and higher for shorter holdings, was withdrawn, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Pension fund tax benefits require the investor to hold until age 60, so the interviewee said investors are encouraged to avoid early withdrawals to keep the tax benefit.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Using an illustration, the interviewee said an investor who puts 6 million in over 25 years from age 35 could end with about 48 million, almost ten times the principal, while the same 6 million put in over 5 years from age 55 grows to about 9.8 million.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Investors in Pakistani mutual funds typically enter around age 45-50, with about 10 years left before retirement, which the interviewee said limits compounding compared with starting at 25-35.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Over 60% of Pakistan's population is under 30, but most wealth is held by people aged 40-60, partly because much of their savings accumulated in the informal sector, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Provident funds are paid out as a cheque to an employee who changes jobs, so the interviewee said savings are often spent, while VPS accounts belong to the individual and are portable, keeping saving systematic.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Mutual fund purchases are possible through bank mobile apps, QuickPay and credit cards, and the interviewee said the State Bank has an initiative to let bank account holders invest directly.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Investors open a bank account for mutual fund purchases and go through AML/KYC again at the fund level, which the interviewee said adds time and cost and can be reduced like the broker onboarding reform.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Lucky Investments is a fully Islamic asset management company, with all its funds Shariah-compliant, and its assets went from zero to about 130 billion, with a claimed fastest-growing record in 2025.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: The interviewee, a CFA who was earlier CEO of Almeezan, said he took over Lucky Investments in late 2024 and that its management team is strong.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: The company's management said it differs from bank-based asset managers by using its diversified industrial group, which spans cement, power, autos, mobile phones, chemicals and textiles, to bring new investors into the industry.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Lucky Investments launched about eight funds in its first year and put a strong focus on technology, with a mobile app and web portal, which the company's management said makes investing easier.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: The interviewee said Almeezan began Pakistan's Islamic fund business and grew from a very small asset manager into the largest in the industry, including conventional managers, over about 30 years.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: Banks account for most fund-channel distribution in Pakistan, and the interviewee said bank-owned asset managers focus on financial-sector investors, while groups like Lucky reach new investors through other channels.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: In April 2026 the number of mutual fund investors in Pakistan rose by about 29,000, the largest monthly increase the guest cited.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)

fact_text: As of 19 May 2026 the guest said mutual fund investors in Pakistan were close to 8.5 lakh, more than the investors at the Pakistan Stock Exchange.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Truth About Pakistani Mutual Funds | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-05-19)
